title: Double Emulsion Generation Using a Polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) Co-axial Flow Focus Device
protocol: Design microfluidic structures for two-layer fabrication using AutoCAD software.
Have the designs printed by a vendor on circuit board film with 10 μm resolution.
Place a pre-cleaned 3 inch diameter silicon wafer on a spin coater and turn on the vacuum to affix it to the chuck.
Apply 1 ml of SU8-3035 in the center of the wafer and spin for 20 sec at 500 rpm, then 30 sec at 2,000 rpm to provide a layer thickness of 50 μm.
Remove the wafer and bake it on a 135 °C hotplate for 30 min.
Allow the wafer to cool to room temperature before moving on to the next step.
Expose the coated wafer to the first layer mask under a collimated 190 mW, 365 nm LED for 90 sec.
Place the wafer on a 135 °C hotplate for 1 min after exposure.
Allow the wafer to cool to room temperature before proceeding to the next step.
Apply 1 ml of SU8-2050 in the center of the wafer and spin for 20 sec at 500 rpm, then 30 sec at 1,375 rpm to result in a layer that provides an additional thickness of 135 μm.
Remove the wafer and bake on a 135 °C hotplate for 30 min, then cool to RT before moving to the next step.
Align the 2nd layer mask onto the geometry patterned in step 1.
Expose the coated wafer to a collimated 190 mW, 365 nm LED for 3 min.
Place the exposed wafer on a 135 °C hotplate for 1 min, then cool to RT before proceeding to the next step.
Immerse the wafer in a stirred bath of propylene glycol monomethyl ether acetate for 30 min to develop the masks.
Wash the wafer in isopropanol and bake on a 135 °C hotplate for 1 min.
Place the developed master in a 100 mm Petri dish for PDMS molding.
Prepare 10:1 PDMS by combining 50 g of silicone base with 5 g of curing agent in a plastic cup.
Mix the contents with a rotary tool fitted with a stir stick.
Degas the mixture inside a desiccator for 30 min, or until all air bubbles are removed.
Pour the PDMS to give a thickness of 3 mm over the master and place back into the desiccator for further degassing.
Once all bubbles are removed, bake the device at 60 °C for 2 hr.
Cut the device from the mold using a scalpel and place it on a clean surface with the patterned side up.
Cut the PDMS mold in half with a razor blade to separate Master 1 from Master 2.
Punch fluidic inlets and outlets with a 0.75 mm biopsy punch on the piece containing the 50 µm fluid handling geometry imprinted by Master 1.
Plasma treat the devices at 1 mbar O2 plasma for 60 sec in a 300 W plasma cleaner.
Wet the surface of the unpunched piece of PDMS with a drop of DI water to temporarily retard PDMS-PDMS bonding and serve as a lubricant.
Place Master 1 on Master 2 surface while viewing through a stereo microscope.
Slide the surfaces relatively until a mechanical lock is achieved when the recessed frames and protruding frames mate.
Place the device in a 60 °C oven and bake the assembled device for two days at 60 °C to evaporate the water and complete bonding.
Fill a 1 ml syringe with distilled water for the inner phase.
Fill a 1 ml syringe with HFE 7500 fluorinated oil containing 1 wt. % biocompatible surfactant for the middle phase.
Fill a 10 ml syringe with a 10 wt. % polyethylene glycol (PEG) in water solution containing 1 wt. % Tween 20 and 1 wt. % sodium dodecyl sulfate for the continuous phase.
Place the microfluidic chip on the stage of an inverted microscope coupled with a digital camera capable of < 100 µsec shutter speeds.
Mount all syringes on syringe pumps.
Attach 27 G needles to the syringes.
Connect ~30 cm lengths of PE-2 tubing to the needles.
Insert loose ends of tubing into appropriate punched holes in the device.
Place a 10 cm length of PE-2 tubing into the exit port of the device and insert the other end in a waste collection container.
Prime the device by running syringe pumps at high rates (2,000 µl/min) until fluid reaches inlet ports of the device.
Focus the microscope on a region containing the 50 µm x 50 µm orifice and downstream exit channel.
Set syringe pumps to deliver fluid to double emulsion generator at flow rates of 250 µl/hr for inner phase, 100 µl/hr for middle phase, and 700 µl/hr for continuous phase.
Wait 10 min for equilibration under these conditions.
Maintain inner and middle phases' flow rates constant at 250 µl/hr and 100 µl/hr, respectively.
Set the outer phase flow rate to 1,050 µl/hr.
Wait 3-5 min for double emulsions generation to stabilize under set flow conditions.
Acquire 5 sec of video images at 30 Hz for offline processing via manual image analysis.
Repeat steps with different flow rates as specified in Table 1.
